title: Colours, and Big and Small
overview:
Say what colour a thing is.
Say if it is big or little.
Put the describing word BEFORE the thing.
A red bag. A big box.
functions: Ask and say what colour a thing is
Say if a thing is big or little
Put a describing word before a thing
Ask which one a person means
Say a thing is good or bad
learningPath: Patterns: the describing word comes first.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 7. Today, colours.
In Unit 6 you named a thing. A bag.
Now you say more. A red bag.
First, the colours. Listen.
Red. Blue. Green. Yellow.
Say them with me. Red. Blue. Green. Yellow.
Black. White. Brown.
Say them with me.
Now, size. Big and little.
A big box. A little box.
Long and short. New and old.
Now the important part. Word order.
In English the describing word comes first.
We say: a red bag.
We do not say: a bag red.
Listen again. A big box. A new pen.
The colour or the size, then the thing.
In many languages it is the other way.
So this one needs practice. Say it many times.
A red bag. A big box. A new pen.
And the question. What colour is it?
It is red. Or: it is a red bag.
Both are right.
Last, two useful words. Good and bad.
This is a good pen. That is a bad pen.
That is Unit 7. Go and describe things.

grammar.title: The describing word comes FIRST
grammar.explanation:
This is the big one today.
English puts the describing word before the thing.
Many languages do the opposite.
grammar.rule:
a red bag        NOT a bag red
a big box        NOT a box big
a new phone      NOT a phone new

a + describing word + thing
a + red + bag
grammar.workedExample:
You have a bag and it is black.
1. Start with a.
2. Then the colour: black.
3. Then the thing: bag.
4. Say: a black bag.
5. Check the order: a, colour, thing.
grammar.mistake:
This is the most common word-order mistake.
No: I have a bag red.
Yes: I have a red bag.
Say it out loud many times until it feels normal.
grammar.practice:
Put them in order.
1. bag / a / blue
2. box / big / a
3. phone / a / new
4. door / green / a
5. table / a / little
6. book / a / good
grammar.answers:
1. a blue bag
2. a big box
3. a new phone
4. a green door
5. a little table
6. a good book
Five or six right? This is the pattern of the unit.

grammar.title: What colour is it?
grammar.explanation:
One question, two good answers.
Both are right. Use the short one when you are quick.
grammar.rule:
What colour is it?
It is red.
It is a red bag.

What colour is your bag?
Black.
It is black.
It is a black bag.
grammar.workedExample:
Someone asks about your coat.
1. They ask: What colour is your coat?
2. Short answer: Blue.
3. Longer: It is blue.
4. Longest: It is a blue coat.
5. All three are correct English.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say: It is colour blue.
The word colour is in the question only.
Yes: It is blue.
grammar.tip: A one-word answer is fine here.
grammar.practice:
Answer about things near you.
1. What colour is your pen?
2. What colour is the door?
3. What colour is this page?
4. What colour is your bag?
grammar.answers:
Any true answer is right.
Check: did you leave out the word colour?
It is blue. Not: It is colour blue.

grammar.title: Big, little, and the others
grammar.explanation:
Size words work the same as colours.
They come before the thing.
They also come after is.
grammar.rule:
Before the thing:  a big box    a little bag
After is:          The box is big.    The bag is little.

big / little
long / short
new / old
full / empty
grammar.workedExample:
Your room is not large.
1. The word is little.
2. You can say it two ways.
3. Before the thing: a little room.
4. After is: My room is little.
5. Both are correct.
grammar.mistake:
After is, you do NOT need a.
No: The box is a big.
Yes: The box is big.
grammar.tip: Two places: before the thing, or after is.
grammar.practice:
Write the sentence two ways.
1. box / big
2. bag / little
3. street / long
4. phone / new
grammar.answers:
1. a big box / The box is big.
2. a little bag / The bag is little.
3. a long street / The street is long.
4. a new phone / The phone is new.
All four? You can describe a thing two ways.

grammar.title: Which one?
grammar.explanation:
When there are two or more, you need which.
It is the question that stops a mistake.
grammar.rule:
Which one do you want?
The red one, please.

Which bag is yours?
The little one.

which = there is more than one
what = you do not know at all
grammar.workedExample:
There are two bags and one is yours.
1. You are asked: Which bag is yours?
2. Do not say the whole thing again.
3. Say the describing word and one.
4. Say: The black one.
5. Or: The little one, please.
grammar.mistake:
Do not say: The black.
English wants the word one after it.
Yes: The black one.
grammar.practice:
Answer each one.
1. Which bag? (the red one)
2. Which box? (the big one)
3. Which pen? (the new one)
4. Which door? (the green one)
grammar.answers:
1. The red one.
2. The big one.
3. The new one.
4. The green one.
All four? You can pick one thing out of many.

readings.title: My Three Bags
readings.passage:
I have three bags.
One is red and it is big.
One is black and it is little.
One is very old.
I take the little black bag to work.
It is not heavy.
The big red bag is for holidays.
The old one stays at home.

readings.title: Which One?
readings.setting: A small shop, by a shelf
readings.passage:
Can I help you?
Yes. I want a bag, please.
Which one? The red one or the black one?
The black one, please.
The big one or the little one?
The little one.
Here you are. It is a good bag.
Thank you. How much is it?
Ten.

readings.title: The Doors
readings.genre: A sign in a big building
readings.passage:
Green door: go in.
Red door: do not go in.

The green door is on the left.
The red door is on the right.
Ask at the desk if you are not sure.

comprehension.q: What colour is the big bag?
comprehension.why: Line 2: One is red and it is big.
Line 5: I take the little black bag to work.

comprehension.q: Why does the little bag go to work?

comprehension.why: Line 2: I want a bag, please.

comprehension.q: Do they want the big one or the little one?
Which door do you go in?
You are not sure which door. What do you do?
comprehension.why: The last line says: ask at the desk.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — Name the colours
speaking.instructions:
Listen and repeat.
red ... blue ... green ... yellow
black ... white ... brown
Now look around you.
Find one thing of each colour. Name it.
Tap the mic. Say seven colours and seven things.
Tap again. Listen back.
Check: colour first, then the thing?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to name a colour. Find that colour near you.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — What colour is it?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: What colour is your bag? B: It is black.
2. A: What colour is the door? B: It is brown.
3. A: What colour is your pen? B: It is blue.
4. A: Nice colour! B: Thank you.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did you leave out the word colour?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor what colour three things are. Answer its questions too.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Big or little?
speaking.instructions:
Describe four things near you.
Say the colour and the size.
Like this: I have a little black bag.
Do your bag, your phone, this room, one more.
Tap the mic. Say four lines.
Check: describing word before the thing?
speaking.tutor: Describe three things to the tutor. Use a colour and a size each time.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Which one?
speaking.instructions:
Read A. Say B.
1. A: Which bag do you want? B: The red one, please.
2. A: The big one or the little one? B: The little one.
3. A: This one? B: Yes, that one. Thank you.
4. A: It is a good bag. B: Yes, it is very nice.
Tap the mic. Say the four B lines.
Check: did you say one after the colour?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to choose between two things. Use which one.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Say it in the right order
speaking.instructions:
Listen. Put the words in order and say it.
1. bag, red, a
2. box, big, a
3. phone, new, a
4. door, green, the
5. bag, little, black, a
6. room, very, big, a
Tap the mic. Say six phrases.
Check: a red bag, a big box, a new phone.
Then: the green door,
a little black bag, a very big room.
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to say three words out of order. Put them right.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — Two describing words
speaking.instructions:
You can use two together.
The size comes before the colour.
a little black bag
a big red box
Now say four of your own.
Tap the mic. Say four phrases.
Check: size first, then colour, then the thing?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to describe a thing with two words. Say one back.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Three things
writing.prompt:
Write three lines.
Describe three things you have.
Put the colour before the thing.
writing.model:
I have a black bag.
I have a blue pen.
I have an old phone.
writing.criteria:
Three lines.
A colour or a size in each one.
The describing word comes before the thing.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Now add a size word to each line: a little black bag.

writing.title: Writing 2 — This room
writing.prompt:
Write four lines about this room.
Say what is here and what colour it is.
writing.model:
The door is brown.
The wall is white.
There is a big table.
There are four little chairs.
writing.criteria:
Four lines about the room.
A colour or a size in each one.
Each line starts with a capital.
Each line ends with a full stop.
writing.extension: Add one line about which thing you like best.

activities.title: Practice 1 — What colour?
activities.instructions:
Name the colour.
1. the sky on a clear day
2. grass
3. milk
4. night
5. a lemon
6. wood
7. blood
8. paper
activities.answers:
1. blue
2. green
3. white
4. black
5. yellow
6. brown
7. red
8. white
Six or more right: good.
activities.solo: Say each one out loud, then check.

activities.title: Practice 2 — Ask and answer
activities.instructions:
Find six things near you.
For each one, ask and answer.
What colour is it? It is ___.
activities.answers:
There is no key here.
Check: did you answer without the word colour?
It is blue, not It is colour blue.
activities.solo: Record all six, then listen back.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Put it in order
activities.instructions:
Put the words in the right order.
1. bag / a / red
2. box / big / a
3. phone / new / a
4. door / the / green
5. table / little / a
6. book / a / good
7. room / big / a / very
8. bag / black / little / a
activities.answers:
1. a red bag
2. a big box
3. a new phone
4. the green door
5. a little table
6. a good book
7. a very big room
8. a little black bag
Six or more right: you have the English order.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Big or little?
activities.instructions:
Choose the right word.
1. A bus is (big / little).
2. A key is (big / little).
3. A phone is (big / little).
4. A house is (big / little).
5. A bottle is (big / little).
6. A table is (big / little).
activities.answers:
1. big
2. little
3. little
4. big
5. little
6. big
Five or six right: good. Some answers can go both ways — say why.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Which one?
activities.instructions:
Answer with: the ___ one.
1. Which bag? (red)
2. Which box? (big)
3. Which pen? (new)
4. Which door? (green)
5. Which bottle? (full)
6. Which chair? (little)
activities.answers:
1. The red one.
2. The big one.
3. The new one.
4. The green one.
5. The full one.
6. The little one.
Five or six right: good. Do not forget the word one.
activities.solo: Say all six out loud, then check.

activities.title: Practice 6 — Read and answer
activities.instructions:
Read My Three Bags again.
1. How many bags?
2. What colour is the big one?
3. Which bag goes to work?
4. Where does the old bag stay?
5. Which bag is for holidays?
activities.answers:
1. Three
2. Red
3. The little black one
4. At home
5. The big red one
Four or five right: you can read a description.
activities.solo: Read it, then answer without looking.

quizzes.q: The sky on a clear day is ___.
quizzes.why: Blue is the colour of a clear sky.
Green is the colour of grass and leaves.

quizzes.q: What colour is it? A good short answer is ___.
quizzes.why: The word colour stays in the question. It is red is enough.

quizzes.q: Which question do you use when there are two bags?
quizzes.why: Which is for choosing between things you can see.
The describing word comes before the thing.
Size, like colour, comes before the thing.

quizzes.q: Put in order: phone / new / a.
quizzes.why: a, then the describing word, then the thing.

quizzes.q: The box has no more space. It is ___.
quizzes.why: Full means there is no more space in it.
Short is the opposite of long. Little is the opposite of big.

quizzes.q: Which bag is yours? Answer: the black ___.
quizzes.why: English wants the word one after the describing word.

quizzes.q: It makes the next word stronger: ___ big.
quizzes.why: Very big is bigger than big.

quizzes.q: Which two words go together as opposites?
quizzes.why: Good and bad are opposites. The others are not pairs.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: Word order is the whole unit
teacherNotes.note: A red bag, not a bag red. Many languages put the describing word after the noun, so this is not carelessness — it is the learner's own grammar showing through. It needs saying out loud many times, not explaining twice. Pattern 1 and Practice 3 are where the time should go.

The colours themselves are easy and most learners half know them already. They are here because they are the safest words to hang the word-order pattern on: the learner can see whether they are right without knowing any grammar.

teacherNotes.type: The black one, not the black
teacherNotes.note: English insists on the word one after a describing word used alone. It sounds like a small thing and it is the difference between sounding like a beginner and sounding fluent in a shop.

teacherNotes.type: Two describing words have an order too
teacherNotes.note: Size before colour: a little black bag, not a black little bag. Speaking 6 touches it. Do not make a rule of it here — a learner who gets one word in the right place has done what this unit asks.

selfAssessment.statement: I can ask what colour a thing is.
I can say a red bag, not a bag red.
I can say if a thing is big or little.
I can ask which one you mean.
I can write about a thing and its colour.

assignment.title: Describe six things
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Describe six things you can see.
Use a colour or a size for each one.
Put the describing word first.
2. Write four lines about this room.
Listen back before you finish. Is the order right every time?
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
